The trip is a metered RydeTAXI with one off-route segment: 18:50–19:00, 6.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.84 km, adding 4.09 km and reaching up to 884 m off the optimal route [F3]. RD-1 places every such unexplained deviation under review, and the remaining +0.51 km of the +4.6 km total excess [F1] is unassigned corridor/matching mileage that RD-2 does not refund, so the recoverable sum is confined to the one segment's extra_km [F1][F3][RD-1][RD-2]. Nothing exempts the segment on traffic grounds: RD-4(a) requires a DataMall incident on the replaced optimal stretch, and F15 records no incidents at all, while the band-2 record for Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway [F12] is a band fact that RD-4(b) says cannot exempt a segment on its own [F15][F12][RD-4].

On consent, the rider's own message came before the segment and was timely: the driver asked at 18:46 about going round "via Defu Avenue 1" [F8] and the rider replied "Can lah, go ahead." at 18:47 [F9], before the 18:50 segment start [F3], with the chat complete and fully timestamped [F10] [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. But the words are a specific named-road agreement, not a general route choice, so under RD-5 it covers driving on Defu Avenue 1 only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road. No fact does: the fact table carries no road name for the driven path, no message places the car on Defu Avenue 1, and no stop there is measured; timing alone does not tie them [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. Nor does the record place the segment somewhere else — the driver's post-trip statement names the same road but is a claim, not consent, and cannot establish the correspondence [F11][RD-5]. The scope of the agreement therefore cannot be read, which is G13's undetermined case, not an exemption. Because the trace's RD-5 test is mechanical (rider message before the segment AND the agreement covers the segment), an undetermined scope is not an exemption and the segment counts [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The amount follows the trace formula: 4.09 km × ($34.39 ÷ 24.39 km = $1.41000/km, as the fare record states it) = $5.7669, rounded to $5.77 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The rider's higher figure of $6.40 rests on F4's 4.54 billed excess kilometres, which exceed the only measured segment and which RD-2 does not refund beyond the segment's extra_km [F4][F3][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting item is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI and RD-3(c) leaves it payable, and there is no surge or unlisted add-on, so no FARE-1 claim arises [F5][F6][F7][RD-3][FARE-1]. No account flag attaches: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days and the driver's record shows 0 upheld route disputes [F18][RD-6]. The result is a partial refund of $5.77 issued as a Ryde voucher, not cash.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 18:50:10 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 18:46 driver: “Traffic ahead on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Defu Avenue 1?”; F9: Chat #2 18:47 rider: “Can lah, go ahead.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked the rider before turning off via Defu Avenue 1 and the rider said can.” (F8, F9, F11)

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the trip ran 24.4 km against an optimal 19.8 km (+4.6 km, +23%), including one off-route segment 18:50–19:00 that drove 6.93 km where the optimal route covers 2.84 km (extra 4.09 km, drifting up to 884 m off the optimal route); this is an unexempted detour segment under RD-1.

This was a RydeTAXI metered trip (fare = base $3.90 + distance $34.39 for 24.39 km at $1.41/km + time + waiting + platform = $50.12), so the detour kilometres flowed straight into the fare; the per-km rate is $1.4100/km, so partial refund = extra_km × $1.41 under RD-2.

The excess-distance billing fact quantifies the overcharge on the billed distance: $6.40 for 4.54 km at the trip's own $1.4100/km rate (F4), which is the meter-based measure of the extra kilometres under RD-2.

The rider's consent was a specific named-road consent only: the driver asked at 18:46 'ok if I go round via Defu Avenue 1?' and the rider replied at 18:47 'Can lah, go ahead.' — before the 18:50–19:00 off-route segment started, so consent is timely, but it reaches only driving on Defu Avenue 1.

No fact in the record ties the 18:50–19:00 driven segment (6.93 km, up to 884 m off the optimal route) to Defu Avenue 1: there is no route-name fact, no location message and no stop on that road, so the correspondence between the agreed road and the segment actually driven is undetermined under G13 / RD-5.

The driver's justification cannot rest on traffic: the only congestion record is Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway band 2 (10–19 km/h) which ended at 18:50, no traffic incidents were recorded near the route at all (F15), and a band fact alone cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b) — so the detour is not excused under RD-4.

The driver's written statement that 'I asked the rider before turning off via Defu Avenue 1' (F11) is a post-trip claim and cannot supply consent for the route actually driven, since only the rider's own pre-segment message counts (F9, which named Defu Avenue 1 only).

The delay and distance are disproportionate to the consent given: the trip took 39.8 min against an estimated 28.3 min (+11.5 min) and 24.4 km against 19.8 km (+23%), which is the signature of a route change beyond the named-road detour rather than of the agreed 'go round via Defu Avenue 1'.

The driver's profile shows 3 disputes with 1 upheld in 90 days (route disputes 0), which is an additional-action basis only; it does not alone establish this detour and does not meet the RD-6 '≥1 upheld route dispute then this case' trigger on the record as it stands.

The trip is a metered RydeTAXI with no published-tariff extras beyond the meter: the waiting item is $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min, a meter waiting unit) and there is no surge (1.0×), so nothing in the bill is a non-tariff add-on; the only recoverable sum is the detour kilometre charge.

weaknesses: The rider did consent in writing before the segment: F9 ('Can lah, go ahead.' at 18:47) follows the driver's F8 question about Defu Avenue 1 at 18:46, and the off-route segment starts at 18:50 (F3) — so RD-5 timeliness is satisfied and the driver will argue the whole 4.09 km segment was authorised; my case therefore depends on the G13 correspondence gap (no fact ties the driven segment to Defu Avenue 1), and the judge may instead read the consent as covering the route round that area.

F12 supports the driver's stated reason for suggesting a reroute (Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway was at band 2 during 18:24–18:50), and while RD-4(b) says a band fact alone cannot exempt a segment, the judge may treat the traffic situation as reasonable-cause context even though F15 records no incident near the route.

The refund under RD-2 is only the mileage portion: the 4.54 km of excess billed distance at $1.41/km (F4) gives at most about $6.40, and any difference between F4's 4.54 km and the segment's 4.09 km (F3) is corridor/matching noise that is not refundable, so the client's expectation of a large fare reduction is not supported.
The waiting item ($0.11, F5) is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI (RD-3(c)) and is not refundable, and there is no surge or non-published add-on (F6, F7) to attack under FARE-1.

RD-6 flag_account is not available on the facts: the driver's 90-day record shows only 1 upheld dispute and 0 upheld route disputes (F18), so the driver's history cannot be used to characterise this as a repeated route violation.

The rider gave consent in his own written message before the segment started: F9 (18:47) 'Can lah, go ahead.' answers F8 (18:46), in which I proposed the named road 'Defu Avenue 1'; the consent message predates the segment start of 18:50 in F3, satisfying RD-5's 'before' test, and F10 confirms the chat is complete with every message timestamped.

The rider's complaint ('was that even the road he said?') is a query about correspondence, not a denial of consent, and F11 shows my account of the exchange matches the chat record, so the chat facts F8/F9 must be read as the rider's own pre-segment authorization of the Defu Avenue 1 routing.

Any refund must be measured only on the unexempt segment's meter excess, and the fare table shows the distance component is 4.54 km billed = $6.40 at $1.4100/km (F4), which is the maximum calculable figure the rider could recover for the single segment, not the $50.12 total in F7.

The duration and distance overage is explained by real congestion on the expressway the rider was told about: F12 records Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 18:24–18:50, matching the reason given in F8, with F2 (+11.5 min) showing the trip was slowed rather than idled.

The only additional charge items on this metered trip are the meter distance, time, waiting of $0.11 (F5, 0.4 min) and the published platform fee of $1.47 (F7); nothing unlisted or manually added appears, so FARE-1 is not engaged and no fee_waived or refund is due on the fare breakdown.

If the segment is found exempt under RD-5, no refund arises and the account history in F18 (1 upheld dispute, 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days) does not meet RD-6's 'route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1' condition, so no flag_account should attach.

weaknesses: F3 shows the driven segment reached up to 884 m from the optimal route, which is well beyond a minor matching wobble; the other side will argue the 6.93 km drive is a genuine 4.09 km detour and RD-1 places the burden of explaining every unexplained deviation on me.

RD-5 requires the consent to cover this specific named road, and G13 warns that mere time order does not prove the car actually travelled on Defu Avenue 1 — there is no fact tying the driven path to Defu Avenue 1, so the judge may find the consent's reach undetermined and the segment unexempt.

F13 records Tampines Expressway at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) and F14 East Coast Parkway at band 5 (40–49 km/h) during the trip window, and F15 shows no traffic incidents at all; that supports the rider's reading that the alternate corridor was not strongly congested and undercuts a 'reasonable cause' defence under RD-4(a).

F18 records 3 disputes against me in 90 days (1 upheld), so the rider will press RD-6 repeated-violation language and the profile history can support a flag_account request even if the segment is exempted.
